Container.Name: roost-socket-proxy
Container.Overview: A filtered, read-mostly view of this server's Docker for roost: list and inspect containers and images, read logs, and start, stop and restart containers. It can't create containers, exec into them, delete anything or change images, so roost can't use it to take over the host. Put it and roost on their own Docker network (roost-ops) and publish no ports. See roost's docs/host-access.md.
Container.Requires: Create the network first, in the Unraid terminal: docker network create roost-ops. Then set roost's Network Type to roost-ops too, and in roost's Secrets page add DOCKER_HOST = tcp://roost-socket-proxy:2375. Don't publish a port and don't add other containers to roost-ops: anything that can reach this proxy gets the access below.

Config.Name: Docker socket
Config.Description: The host's Docker socket. The proxy is the only thing that touches it.

Config.Name: POST
Config.Description: Keep 0. 1 allows creating containers, which is full control of the host.

Config.Name: Containers (read)
Config.Description: List and inspect containers. Note: inspect shows each container's environment variables.

Config.Name: Restart / stop / kill
Config.Description: Restart, stop and kill containers (works with POST=0).

Config.Name: Info
Config.Description: docker info: engine version, storage driver, counts.

Config.Name: Exec
Config.Description: Keep 0. Exec is a shell in any container, including ones with host mounts.

Config.Name: Archive
Config.Description: Keep 0. Copies files out of (and into) containers.

Config.Name: Export
Config.Description: Keep 0. Exports a container's whole filesystem.

Config.Name: Volumes
Config.Description: List volumes. Harmless read-only, but rarely needed.
